fluidSubstrates.name: Fresh Cloudy Apple Cider (High Polyphenol & Pectin Cloud, Turbidity 420 NTU, α_254 = 28.5 cm⁻¹)
fluidSubstrates.targetPathogen: Escherichia coli O157:H7 & Cryptosporidium parvum oocysts
fluidSubstrates.photoreactivationSusceptibility: Moderate: Requires post-UV dark holding tank or immediate opaque cold packaging to prevent photolyase enzyme activation
fluidSubstrates.description: Unfiltered raw apple juice with suspended pectin, starches, and polyphenols that heavily absorb and scatter 254 nm germicidal radiation; requires thin-film annular geometry or Dean vortex turbulence.

fluidSubstrates.name: Clarified White Grape Must (Low Turbidity 14 NTU, α_254 = 8.2 cm⁻¹)
fluidSubstrates.photoreactivationSusceptibility: Low: Spoilage yeasts exhibit negligible blue-light photolyase photoreactivation in acidic high-osmotic must
fluidSubstrates.description: Enzymatically depectinized and settled grape juice with excellent UV penetration, allowing effective non-thermal stabilization against wild fermentation yeasts prior to inoculating selected wine yeast strains.

fluidSubstrates.name: Commercial Liquid Sucrose Syrup (67.5 °Brix, Viscosity 160 cP, Low Absorption α_254 = 3.4 cm⁻¹)
fluidSubstrates.photoreactivationSusceptibility: Negligible: Low water activity (aw < 0.85) permanently suppresses cellular DNA repair mechanisms
fluidSubstrates.description: Dense industrial liquid sweetener requiring high back-pressure and heated inlet (35°C) to lower dynamic viscosity and ensure laminar shear over the quartz sleeve without channeling.

fluidSubstrates.name: Dairy Milk Permeate / Sweet Whey (Riboflavin Sensitizer, α_254 = 42.0 cm⁻¹)
fluidSubstrates.substrateCategory: Dairy Stream with Dissolved Lactose & Salts (pH 6.3, 5.2 °Brix)
fluidSubstrates.targetPathogen: Listeria monocytogenes & Bacillus cereus vegetative cells
fluidSubstrates.photoreactivationSusceptibility: High: Native riboflavin acts as a photosensitizer; fluid requires strictly shielded dark storage to prevent lipid light-oxidation off-flavors
fluidSubstrates.description: Ultrafiltration permeate rich in dissolved riboflavin (vitamin B2) which creates an intense optical absorption barrier at 254 nm and 365 nm, necessitating ultra-thin film (< 1.0 mm) passage.

fluidSubstrates.name: Craft Raw Kombucha Tea (Acetic Acid Bacteria, Turbidity 95 NTU, α_254 = 16.5 cm⁻¹)
fluidSubstrates.targetPathogen: Salmonella enterica & Excessive Brettanomyces wild yeast
fluidSubstrates.photoreactivationSusceptibility: Moderate: Low pH suppresses nucleotide excision repair; immediate cold kegging ensures biological stability
fluidSubstrates.description: Live probiotic tea broth containing polyphenols, organic acids, and yeast sediment; pulsed UV-C provides target microbial lethality without pasteurizing beneficial heat-sensitive organic acids.

targetPathogens.name: Escherichia coli O157:H7 (STEC Shiga Toxin-Producing)
targetPathogens.classification: Gram-Negative Enteric Bacterium (FDA 21 CFR § 120 Juice HACCP Target)
targetPathogens.primaryDamageMechanism: Cyclobutane Pyrimidine Dimers (CPDs, mainly thymine-thymine dimers) halting DNA replication fork
targetPathogens.photoreactivationCapacity: High: Contains phr gene photolyase enzyme; repaired by 350-450 nm blue light photons unless dose ≥ 30 mJ/cm²

targetPathogens.name: Cryptosporidium parvum (Thick-Walled Environmental Oocysts)
targetPathogens.primaryDamageMechanism: High susceptibility to UV-C nucleic acid cross-linking; renders sporozoites non-infective in mammalian host cells
targetPathogens.photoreactivationCapacity: Negligible: Cryptosporidium oocysts lack photolyase repair machinery, preventing infectivity restoration

targetPathogens.name: Salmonella enterica (Multiple Serovars incl. Typhimurium & Enteritidis)
targetPathogens.primaryDamageMechanism: Formation of 6-4 photoproducts (6-4PPs) and CPDs inducing fatal single-strand and double-strand DNA scission
targetPathogens.photoreactivationCapacity: Moderate: Inactivated photolyase repair kinetics under dark post-treatment holding conditions

targetPathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes (Gram-Positive Psychrotroph)
targetPathogens.classification: Gram-Positive Foodborne Pathogen with Peptidoglycan Cell Wall
targetPathogens.primaryDamageMechanism: Thick peptidoglycan wall slightly attenuates UV penetration, requiring higher delivered fluence to dimerize genomic DNA
targetPathogens.photoreactivationCapacity: Low: Possesses limited photolyase activity; highly susceptible to permanent photolytic inactivation

targetPathogens.name: Human Norovirus / Murine Norovirus (MNV-1 Single-Stranded RNA)
targetPathogens.classification: Non-Enveloped Viral Pathogen (Low Infectious Dose Gastrointestinal Agent)
targetPathogens.primaryDamageMechanism: Photochemical cross-linking of viral capside proteins and viral (+)ssRNA genome cleavage
targetPathogens.photoreactivationCapacity: Zero: Lacks any intrinsic repair enzymes or metabolic machinery outside host cells
